name: Mountain Climber
summary: A dynamic bodyweight movement performed from a high plank position, rapidly driving the knees toward the chest to build core stability and cardiovascular endurance.

setup: Place your hands flat on the floor directly beneath your shoulders with fingers spread slightly.
Extend your legs behind you onto the balls of your feet, establishing a solid high plank position.
Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and maintain a straight line from your head to your heels.
steps: Drive one knee forward toward your chest in a straight line without letting your hips pike upward.
Quickly switch legs by extending the front leg back while simultaneously driving the opposite knee toward your chest.
Continue alternating legs in a smooth, rhythmic running motion while keeping your shoulders stacked over your wrists.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously and rhythmically throughout the set, avoiding holding your breath.

common_faults.fault: Piking the hips up into a pike or downward dog position.
common_faults.correction: Keep your core braced and shoulders directly over your wrists to maintain a flat plank profile.

common_faults.fault: Letting the lower back sag into hyperextension.
common_faults.correction: Engage your abdominal wall and slightly tuck your pelvis to keep the lumbar spine neutral.

common_faults.fault: Bouncing aggressively off the toes, rocking the upper body forward and back.
common_faults.correction: Isolate the movement to the lower body, keeping the torso and shoulder girdle completely stable.

precautions: Ensure the floor surface is non-slip so your hands and feet do not slide during dynamic movement.
